owner.occupation: Paper conservator at a university library

world.bio: I'm a paper conservator at a university library in New York. I trained in Western paper and parchment conservation: book repair, mould treatment, deacidification, paste and Japanese tissue mending. I've been at the library for eleven years. Lately we were handed a donated collection of Chinese stone rubbings and albums, and I know I cannot treat them alone.
skills_assets: Conservation lab with fume hood, suction table, humidification chamber, light table
Experience with Western rag paper, parchment, early printed books
Training in Japanese tissue mending and wheat starch paste
Access to the library's special collections catalogue and cataloguers
A network of American paper conservators; no East Asian specialists

projects.name: Chinese rubbings and albums
projects.text: The library received a donation of about 300 Chinese stone rubbings and two albums. Several have flaking paste and silverfish damage. I have catalogued about 60 and photographed 30. The albums are the priority: folded accordion style with tipped-in sheets. I need an East Asian paper specialist.

projects.name: Visiting specialist fund
projects.text: My department has a small visiting-specialist fund that must be spent by next June. I've drafted a proposal but haven't named a person. The fund covers travel, accommodation and a day rate.

projects.name: Apartment renovation in Queens
projects.text: Kitchen tile and a new bathroom vanity. The contractor is two weeks late. I'm living with plastic sheets over the doorway.

notes.text: Opened the second box of rubbings today. The first sheet has a faint insect trail through the ink, like a map. Quite beautiful, quite alarming.
Silverfish evidence in album one. Froze it for two weeks. Not sure about the paste; it is flaking in a way I don't recognise from Western starch.

Called a colleague at the Met. She said East Asian mounting is a separate discipline: the paste, the backing papers, the mounting sequence, even the brushes. She suggested I find someone who trained in China, Japan or Taiwan.
The cat's insulin schedule is wrecking my sleep. 7am and 7pm. I can't travel more than a day without a sitter.
Rehearsal for the community orchestra. We're doing Dvorak. My viola section is four people and one of them keeps coming in early.
The head of special collections asked how long the Chinese collection will take. I said it depends on whether I can find a specialist. She said the donor is keen to see it exhibited next spring.
Looked at conference programmes for paper conservators. Plenty on Western books; almost nothing about East Asian rubbings.
Contractor says the tile will arrive Friday. Again.
Wrote a draft email to a few people asking for names. Didn't send. Don't want to sound like I'm admitting I can't do it.
Opened the second album. Beautiful calligraphy. Some pages have been repaired with what looks like cellophane tape. Heartbreaking.

messages.text: Marjorie: How are the Chinese rubbings coming along? Me: Slow. I'm cataloguing first. Marjorie: The donor wants an update. Me: I'll send photos next week.
Colleague: You need someone who knows East Asian mounting. Me: Do you know anyone? Colleague: I know a couple in Taiwan and Shanghai, but I'd have to ask. Me: Please do.
Luis: The tile comes Friday. Me: That's what you said last week. Luis: This time it's on the truck.
Friend: Are you coming to the Saturday rehearsal? Me: Yes, if the cat is stable. Friend: Bring your viola.
Admin: Reminder that the visiting fund lapses on 30 June. Me: I know. Admin: Do you have a candidate? Me: Not yet.

Fund must be spent by next June
